(e) Charges Framed Section 411/482 IPC (f) Plea of accused Pleaded not guilty (g) Final Order Acquitted (h) Date of institution 08.03.2018 (i) Date when judgment was 13.10.2023  reserved (j) Date of judgment 19.10.2023  BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 1.
Present charge-sheet has been forwarded by the SHO, PS Shakarpur against the accused to face trial for the offences under Section 379/411/482 IPC.

2. In nutshell, the case of the prosecution is that a FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.1/8 Digitally signed by SONIKA SONIKA Date:
2023.10.19 14:01:29 +0530 complaint was made by the complainant regarding theft of his motorcycle bearing no. UP 16U 2725 and as a result, the FIR was registered u/s 379 IPC.

Thereafter, on 20.09.2015 at about 20:05 p.m., at Khirwa Chopala in front of Bharat Gas Service Godown, PS Khankarkhera, Meerut, UP, the accused was found in possession of aforesaid stolen motorcycle which the accused was retaining or received dishonestly and knowing or having reason to believe that the same to be a stolen property and he was using a fake number plate bearing no. UP 15AW 4810 in place of original one.
Consequently, after completion of investigation, the final report (charge sheet) for the offences under Section 379/411/482 IPC was forwarded against accused.

4. After hearing the parties, charge was served upon accused for the commission of offence under Section 411/482 IPC v.o.d. 20.09.2018 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
5. Thereafter, matter was listed for Prosecution's evidence.
It is pertinent to mention here that several attempts were made to serve the summons upon the complainant Sh. Saurabh Singh, but the process was SONIKA

Thereafter, summons was ordered to be served through DCP concerned but again,
the same were also received back unserved and hence the witness was dropped from the list of witnesses.

6. Prosecution in support of its case examined 02 witnesses.
7. PW-1 ASI Ram Kishore deposed that on 20.01.2017, he was posted as ASI at PS Shakarpur and on that day, the investigation of present case was assigned to him by the SHO as the initial IO of the case was transferred.
He further deposed that he collected the case file from the MHC(R) concerned and gone through the same.

He further deposed that during the course of investigation, some documents pertaining to case FIR No. 734/2015 u/s 411,420, 413 & 414 IPC of PS Kankarkhera,
Distt. Meerut, UP through Dak, he gone through the said documents.

He further deposed that as per information received from the documents pertaining to afore-said case FIR, it came to light that the stolen motorcycle pertaining to present case FIR No. 31/2015 PS Shakarpur had been recovered by the UP police during the course of investigation of that case.

He further deposed that on 16.05.2017,
he visited PS Kankarkhera, Distt. Meerut, UP and contacted the IO of case FIR No. 734/15.

He further deposed that he made inquiries from him at length and during the course of investigation, it came to know that the accused has already been released on bail by the court concerned in that case.

He further deposed that he collected the fake number plate Digitally signed by FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.3/8SONIKA SONIKA Date:
2023.10.19 14:01:43 +0530 bearing registration no. of the bike as UP-15AW-4810 instead of UP-16U-2725 and he seized the said no. plate vide memo Ex. PW1/A.

He further deposed that he also collected the stolen motorcycle bearing registration no.
UP- 16U-2725 vide memo Ex.PW1/B.
He further deposed that he brought the motorcycle to PS Shakarpur and deposited the same with the MHC(M).

He further deposed that on 10.08.2017, he again visited to PS Kankarkhera, UP and visited the residence of accused Sonu @ Laxman alongwith local police village Pawali khurd but the accused was not found present there, however, the family members of the accused were asked to apprise the accused to participate in the investigation.

He further deposed that on 22.09.2017, the accused was granted anticipatory bail in the present case by the concerned Sessions Court and on 11.10.2017, the accused alongwith Court order visited to him in the PS where he arrested him formally vide memo Ex. PW1/C and as per Court order, he was released on anticipatory bail after his arrest.
He further deposed that on completion of investigation into the present matter, he prepared the chargesheet against the accused and filed the same before the concerned Court for his trial.
He further identified the accused.

He further deposed that the documents collected by him (certified copies of a letter of SSP, Meerut, FIR No. 734/15 and other relevant documents running into 19 pages) available on record and same are SONIKA Date:
2023.10.19 14:01:51 +0530 FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.4/8 Ex.PW1/D (colly).

Thereafter, the witness correctly identified the stolen motorcycle bearing registration no. UP-16U-2725 from photographs available on record Ex. P1 to P4 and also identified the number plate registration no. UP-15AW-4810, Ex. P5.
PW-1
was cross-
examined at length by Ld. counsel for accused.

8. PW-2 ASI Pramod Kumar deposed that on 04.01.2015, he was posted as HC at PS Shakarpur and on that day, the present case was registered on the basis of complaint of complainant namely Saurav Singh by SI Arvind and thereafter, the investigation was assigned to him.
He further deposed that he flashed messages to SCRB, WT messages & NCRB in terms of incident of present case.

He further deposed that on the same day, he alongwith complainant visited the spot, inspected the same,
prepared the site plan of the spot in the presence of complainant Ex.PW2/A.
He further deposed that no clue about recovery of stolen vehicle and arrest of the accused came to light, hence, the matter was filed as untraced.
PW- 2 was not cross-
examined on behalf of accused despite opportunity.

9. It was noted that as the material witness i.e. the complainant was not traceable, carrying on with further prosecution evidence and procedure would be a futile exercise as well as wastage of judicial time and resources.

The prosecution could never be able to prove beyond reasonable doubts that the motorcycle recovered from the possession of the accused was received or retained by him Digitally signed by SONIKA FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.5/8SONIKA Date:
2023.10.19 14:01:56 +0530 dishonestly and having knowledge of the same to be stolen property or the same is the one qua which the present FIR was registered.

Hence, PE was closed v.o.d. 06.10.2023.
Statement of accused U/Sec. 281 Cr.P.C was recorded wherein accused denied all the incriminating evidence put to him and stated that he is innocent and has committed no offence as alleged.
Since, the accused did not opt to lead defence evidence, the matter was listed for final arguments.
11. It was argued by the Ld. APP for the State that the prosecution witnesses have successfully proved the factum of commission of offence by the accused, beyond reasonable doubt.
He further stated that all the witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution and hence, the accused is liable to be convicted and punished as per law.
12. On the other hand, it was argued by Ld. Counsel for accused, the accused was falsely implicated in the case.
He further argued that there are several discrepancies and material contradictions in the deposition of the prosecution witnesses which create grave suspicion about the prosecution's case.

He prayed that the accused deserve to Digitally signed by SONIKA FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.6/8SONIKA Date:
2023.10.19 14:02:02 +0530 be acquitted in this case.
13.
I have heard the arguments addressed by Ld. APP for the State and Ld. Counsel for the accused and have carefully perused the material available on record.
14. It is a settled legal principle that the prosecution has to prove its case against the accused beyond all reasonable doubts and has to stand upon its own legs.
The burden of proof in a criminal trial always rests upon the prosecution and the same never shifts on the accused.

15. In the present case, the accused persons have been charged for the offences punishable U/Sec.
411/482 IPC.

Since the testimony of the complainant could not be recorded as he was untraceable and was consequently dropped from the list of witnesses, it could not be proved that the motorcycle which was stolen and allegedly recovered from the accused belonged to the complainant for which the present case FIR was lodged in the police station.
16. So far as offence U/Sec.482 IPC is concerned, it is alleged that the accused was found in possession of a stolen motorcycle and was using false/fake registration number plate on the said vehicle.
It is noted that all the prosecution witnesses of the alleged recovery, are police official.
No independent/public witness has been cited as a witness to the alleged recovery which casts a serious doubt on the fairness of investigation.

In the absence of independent witness, the testimony of the police witnesses is not SONIKA Date:
FIR No. 31/2015 State Vs. Sonu @ Laxman Page no.7/8 sufficient to hold the accused guilty of offence U/Sec. 482 IPC.
17.

sentences.text: Hence, the prosecution has failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt, that the stolen vehicle was recovered from the possession of the accused and that when the said vehicle was recovered, it had false/fake number plate, which was being used by the accused.

There is no other independent State vs Sonu @ Laxman on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42255191/
4 witness to the recovery in the present case.
The other witnesses are police officials/formal witnesses and their examination could have been supplementary step to join the link of investigation and the sequence of events.
But, in the absence of examination of material witness i.e. the complainant, the other witnesses are of no help to the prosecution.
18. In the light of aforesaid facts and circumstances, I hold that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of the offences under Sections 411/482 IPC against accused.

Consequently,
accused namely Sonu @ Laxman stands acquitted from the offences under Section 411/482 IPC.
